transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Patel, Lina Park, Maya Chen, Ethan Ross, Samir Gupta, Jonah Lee, ~150 employees (virtual)

Summary:
Ava opens the all-hands with a brief Q3 recap, high-level metrics and hiring pause context; Lina covers infra updates including Dedicated region expansion and KV cache improvements; Maya walks through product roadmap priorities and Optimize toolkit; Samir addresses security/compliance progress (SOC 2 recert, KMS integration) and answers questions about Private deployment timelines; Q&A at the end covers hiring, pricing, and reliability.

Topics:
- Q3 metrics & business health
- Dedicated region expansion + infra work
- Private deployment / security status
- Product roadmap and Optimize features
- Sales momentum and enterprise deals
- Hiring and org updates

Action items (read out):
- Lina to publish infra rollout timeline
- Maya to post roadmap doc and recording link
- Jonah to update on-call schedule
- Ethan to distribute sales playbook

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Ava Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, welcome to our October all-hands. Quick housekeeping, recording's on, chat's open, we'll save Q&A till the end.
[00:30] Ava Patel: First, a quick note on Q3; we saw strong usage growth in bookings from our mid-market cohort, um, but net of cost we had some noise from GPU supply pricing near month end. We're balancing spend and hiring — we have a small hiring pause for non-customer-facing roles.
[01:15] Crowd murmur / applause
[01:30] Ava Patel: Our ARR growth this quarter was in the mid-teens, churn roughly flat, and importantly latency SLO attainment improved after the kernel scheduler updates. I'll hand it over to Lina for infra.
[01:45] Lina Park: Thanks. Quick infra update: Dedicated region expansion — we validated CI in two new datacenters and started canaries for the EU/Dedicated pools. There's been some tricky flakiness with the network SR-IOV drivers causing noisy neighbors, so we implemented an isolation patch. The KV cache persistence changes also landed, though there are a few perf regressions in long-tail workloads.
[02:20] Lina Park: We're also rolling out a smarter kernel selector — it picks optimized kernels based on seq len dist and hardware. Some of the telemetry calls it "kernel autopilot" internally. That's the main reason token latency improved.
[03:05] Ethan Ross: Quick sales note — we've closed three new mid-market deals where Dedicated capacity was a gating factor. Customers are choosing Reserved over hosted because of predictable throughput and, um, data isolation. Pricing discussions are ongoing, we'll share playbook updates.
[03:45] Maya Chen: On product, Optimize has a new batching advisor UI, and we're testing quantization recommendation flows. We want customers to see cost/perf tradeoffs easily — for example drop from F32 to int8 variants for non-latency-critical paths.
[04:10] Maya Chen: Also working on structured output improvements and better function-calling ergonomics.
[04:45] Samir Gupta: Security: SOC 2 recertification is on track, evidence collection is 80% complete. KMS/HSM integrations for key management are in private beta; audit logs and RBAC improvements are shipping next sprint. For Private, the VPC onboarding checklist was tightened, and we added network segmentation tests.
[05:30] Samir Gupta: A note on on-prem: latency on some customer hardware varies a lot, we recommend our quantization profiles plus the kernel selector. There's a bit of manual tuning for bespoke racks.
[06:10] Audience question (Slack + Q): Are we doing price increases or packaging changes?
[06:30] Ava Patel: No broad price hikes. We're aligning packaging more tightly with Dedicated commitments and offering new add-ons for observability retention and SLA. We'll communicate changes to customers with 60 days notice.
[07:05] Jonah Lee: Ops update — incident MTTR is down 18% quarter-over-quarter after the new tracing hooks. We still want to get better on cross-region failover tests, and we'll run a game day next month.
[07:40] Lina Park: On the technical roadmap: next quarter we'll focus on further KV cache optimizations to reduce cold-start token cost, and a rework of the batching engine to support latency-aware batching. There might be small regressions during A/B rollout.
[08:20] Ava Patel: Hiring — we remain focused on critical roles: Platform SRE, Inference Engineers, and Product Managers for Optimize. We are pausing a few non-critical IC roles for now. If you have questions, talk to your manager.
[09:00] Audience: question about Private rollout timeline
[09:15] Samir Gupta: Timeline — Private GA customers should expect staged rollouts through Q4. For on-prem kits, lead times depend on hardware validation; for VPC we expect customers can onboard in 2-4 weeks once approvals are done.
[10:00] Audience: question about SOC 2 evidence access for customers
[10:15] Samir Gupta: We'll produce a vendor pack and a security whitepaper, and we'll share a sanitized audit evidence bundle for enterprise prospects under NDA.
[11:00] Audience: question re: model catalog and open model support
[11:20] Maya Chen: Model catalog expanded — we added two community-curated LLMs with performance profiles; note that some names in the transcript might be garbled, e g, "Redwood Dedicate" in notes is "Redwood Dedicated". We'll maintain verified perf profiles in the docs.
[12:30] Ethan Ross: Sales momentum — enterprise pipeline is growing, we're seeing more trials convert when we can run benchmarks with customer prompt sets. Reminder to sales, coordinate with SEs early to run those perf runs.
[13:10] Ava Patel: Ok let's go through rapid-fire Q&A from Slack — I'm going to call out a few themes: compensation, return-to-office, and product feedback loops.
[13:50] Audience member (mic): Can we get more visibility into per-route token costs?
[14:05] Lina Park: Yes, Console will show token-level cost breakdowns per route soon; ETA mid-November. The initial UI is in staging.
[14:40] Audience: question on competitors — are we worried about managed endpoints from large clouds?
[15:00] Ava Patel: We're focused on differentiation: unified runtime, cost-aware controls, and predictable Dedicated offerings. Clouds compete on scale but not necessarily the production-grade runtime features our customers need.
[15:30] Closing remarks from Ava: Thanks team, please review the action items, and managers will schedule follow-ups where needed. We'll post recording and deck by end of day.

Q&A snippets / imperfect transcriptions follow: 
[16:00] Speaker 1: "Will RBAC changes require reconfig of SSO?"
[16:12] Samir Gupta: "No, SAML/S S O integrations won't change, it's an opt-in RBAC layer. We do need to map groups for least privilege."
[16:50] Speaker 2: "Any change to caching ttl defaults?"
[17:02] Lina Park: "We're increasing default prefix cache ttl for hosted workloads but not for Dedicated by default, it's configurable."
[18:30] Speaker 3: "How will Optimize advices be surfaced?"
[18:45] Maya Chen: "Advisor UI in Console and an API endpoint for programmatic suggestions; initially suggestions are experimental and not auto-applied."
[19:30] Closing: recording and deck to be posted, action items repeated.

References / Links mentioned in call:

- Infra rollout timeline (will be published by Lina)
- SOC 2 evidence pack (internal/security)

End of transcript.
